description: Hawaii-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Hawaii's statewide speed statute, section 291C-102, makes a driver violate the speed law by exceeding
options: The maximum set by county ordinance or by the director's official signs
25 mph in every residential district whether or not a sign or ordinance exists
questions.explanation: Section 291C-102 does not set a numeric statewide urban, rural, or interstate default. It applies where the maximum or minimum speed limit is established by county ordinance or by official signs placed by the director of transportation on highways under the director's jurisdiction.

questions.q: Hawaii's excessive-speeding offense in section 291C-105 is driving faster than
options: The limit by 30+ mph, or 80+ mph
The posted limit by any amount
questions.explanation: Section 291C-105(a) prohibits a speed exceeding the applicable state or county speed limit by 30 miles per hour or more, or 80 miles per hour or more irrespective of the applicable limit. The applicable limit means one set by county ordinance, by official signs of the director of transportation, or for school zones and construction areas under section 291C-104.

questions.q: Hawaii's school-zone speed limit is
options: A statewide 15 mph whenever children are outside
A statewide 25 mph during school hours
Whatever the state or county sets for that zone
45 mph unless a beacon is flashing
questions.explanation: Section 291C-104(b) requires the director of transportation and the counties, in their jurisdictions, to establish maximum speed limits for school zones and construction areas. The director places official signs in school zones. The statute does not set one statewide school-zone number.

questions.q: If a driver in a Hawaii school zone or construction area exceeds the established maximum by 30 mph or more, or drives 80 mph or more, the statute says
options: The school-zone section still controls the offense
The violation is only a parking offense
No speed law applies inside a construction area
questions.explanation: Section 291C-104(a) says that if the person drives more than 30 miles an hour over the maximum established for the school zone or construction area, or at 80 miles per hour or more, section 291C-105 controls.

questions.q: In a Hawaii prosecution under section 291E-61, which result within three hours is competent evidence that the person was under the influence of an intoxicant?
options: .05 or less grams of alcohol per 210 liters of breath
.08 or more per 100 ml blood or 210 liters breath
questions.explanation: Section 291E-3(a) makes .08 or more grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters or cubic centimeters of blood, or per 210 liters of breath, within three hours after the alleged violation, competent evidence that the person was under the influence for a prosecution under section 291E-61 or 291E-61.5.

questions.q: If a Hawaii alcohol test shows .05 or less grams per 100 milliliters of blood, or .05 or less grams per 210 liters of breath, section 291E-3 says
options: The person is presumed under the influence
The person is presumed not under the influence
The under-21 measurable-amount rule is proved
questions.explanation: Section 291E-3 states that presumption for .05 or less. A result above .05 but below .08 may be considered with other evidence and does not by itself create a presumption. It shall be presumed that the defendant was not under the influence of alcohol at the time of the alleged violation.

questions.q: A person under 21 in Hawaii may not operate a vehicle
options: With a measurable amount of alcohol
Only if the test is within two hours and shows .05
questions.explanation: Section 291E-64(a) says it is unlawful for any person under the age of twenty-one to operate any vehicle with a measurable amount of alcohol.

questions.q: When a Hawaii district judge finds that traffic violations within a 12-month period show disrespect for the law and disregard for safety, section 286-128(d) provides that the licensee
options: Loses the license automatically for one year at a fixed point total
Must report in person for a record review; retraining may be ordered
Receives a warning letter at 8 points
Is barred as a habitual offender after six tickets
questions.explanation: Section 286-128(d) in the 2017 compilation uses that frequency standard within a twelve-month period. At the review, the judge may order a course of instruction in driver retraining.

questions.q: A Hawaii instruction permit may be issued to a person aged
questions.explanation: Section 286-110(a) allows a person aged fifteen years and six months or more, who would otherwise qualify except for lack of instruction, to apply for an instruction permit. Except for a motor scooter or motorcycle, section 286-110(e) requires a licensed person 21 or older in the passenger seat beside the permit holder.

questions.q: If a Hawaii instruction-permit holder under 18 drives between 11:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m., the licensed person beside the driver must be
questions.explanation: Section 286-110(e) requires the parent or guardian to occupy the seat beside an under-18 permit holder during those hours, unless the permit holder is an emancipated minor, and that person must be licensed for the same category of vehicle. All occupants must be restrained by a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.q: A Hawaii provisional license for a person at least 16 and under 18 requires that the person has held an instruction permit for at least
options: Six months of a full license
questions.explanation: Section 286-102.6(a): an applicant at least 16 and under 18 must have held the instruction permit for 180 days, with no pending proceeding that might suspend or revoke it, and must complete the requirements of sections 286-108 and 286-109.

questions.q: Without a licensed parent or guardian supervising, a Hawaii provisional licensee shall not transport more than one person under 18 unless that person is
questions.explanation: Section 286-102.6(b)(3) states that passenger limit and those household-member exceptions. All occupants must be restrained by safety belts or a child restraint.

questions.q: A Hawaii provisional licensee driving between 11:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. must have a licensed parent or guardian in the front seat unless
options: Going to work or a school activity with a signed note
Any licensed friend over 18 is available by phone
questions.explanation: Section 286-102.6(c) states those two conditions. Even then, the licensee shall not transport more than one person under 18 between 11:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. without a licensed parent or guardian. The licensee is going to or from work with a signed employer statement, or to or from a school-authorized activity with a signed parent or guardian statement.

questions.q: In Hawaii, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Hawaii issues a learner's permit for a car at 15½ years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Hawaii car permit: 15½ years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Hawaii, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Hawaii requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: HRS §286-102.6 Provisional license for persons under the age of eighteen

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Hawaii complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Hawaii requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: HAR Title 19 Chapter 139 Driver Education Program Requirements

questions.q: Of a Hawaii teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Hawaii requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Hawaii: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: HAR Title 19 Chapter 139 Driver Education Program Requirements

questions.q: In Hawaii, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Hawaii, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Hawaii not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Hawaii restricts provisional drivers from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Hawaii new drivers: off the road 11 p.m. to 5 a.m..

provenance.manual: HRS §286-102.6 Provisional license for persons under the age of eighteen

questions.q: In Hawaii, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Hawaii drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Hawaii car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Hawaii car knowledge test has 30 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Hawaii car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Hawaii car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Hawaii, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Hawaii, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Hawaii, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

provenance.manual: HRS §291E-61 Operating a vehicle under the influence of an intoxicant

questions.q: In Hawaii, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Hawaii sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Hawaii, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Hawaii brings a suspension of 2 years.
questions.remember: Hawaii, first refusal: 2 years without a license.

provenance.manual: HRS §291E-41 Administrative revocation of license and privilege to operate a vehicle

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Hawaii?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Hawaii can be posted up to 60 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Hawaii rural interstate: up to 60 mph.

provenance.manual: HRS §291C-106 Speed limit for Daniel K. Inouye highway

questions.q: Which best describes Hawaii's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Hawaii: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Hawaii?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Hawaii, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Hawaii left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Hawaii's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Hawaii seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: HRS §291-11.6 Mandatory use of seat belts, when, penalty

questions.q: What is Hawaii's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Hawaii requires at least $40,000 / $80,000 / $20,000.
